headline: Test D (Otázka dne) fails its stop rule: 1 opt-in against 30 needed. Overnight: class backup (download/load) for instructors, PR #45.

tests.name: Otázka dne, practised together
tests.stop_rule: fewer than 30 opt-ins, or under 40 % of opt-ins still answering on day 14
tests.source: read-only SELECT on public.events (app = 'zbrojni-kviz', key_action kinds qotd_*), run 2026-11-25; automated browsers are dropped by the client
tests.why: 1 opt-in is far below the 30 the rule requires. The retention half (1 of 1 still answering) says nothing with one participant.
tests.caveat: The test was underpowered: only 14 distinct visitors opened the app in the window, so 30 opt-ins was out of reach whatever the feature did. The result says the audience is too small to test D, not that learners rejected it.
tests.what_stays: The feature stays live as it is (opt-in, costs nothing, no data beyond key_action). Removing it, or reviving the test once traffic grows, is a product call for Pavol.

decisions.question: Test D verdict when the rule's opt-in bar exceeds total traffic
decisions.default_taken: fail, with the underpowered caveat recorded
decisions.why: The stop rule was set in advance; reporting it as written keeps the test honest. The caveat tells Pavol why.

decisions.question: Class backup format
decisions.default_taken: one JSON file (kind zbrojni-kviz-classes), merged by class code, newer summary wins
decisions.why: Survives a cleared browser and moves between devices; no server.

proposals.needs_pavol: Keep it as a quiet opt-in feature, remove it, or rerun the test when traffic is higher (e.g. after test C brings classes). Default if he says nothing: keep, untouched.
